ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points $A$, $O$, and $B$ lie on the same straight line, and $\angle AOC = \angle BOD$. Lines $OM$ and $ON$ are the angle bisectors of $\angle AOC$ and $\angle BOD$, respectively. If $\angle COD = 80^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle MON$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $OM$ and $ON$ are the angle bisectors of $\angle AOC$ and $\angle BOD$ respectively, \\
hence, $\angle MOC = \frac{1}{2}\angle AOC$ and $\angle NOD = \frac{1}{2}\angle BOD$, \\
therefore, $\angle MON = \frac{1}{2}(\angle AOC + \angle BOD) + \angle COD$ \\
$= \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ - \angle COD) + \angle COD$ \\
$= 90^\circ + \frac{1}{2}\angle COD$, \\
since $\angle COD = 80^\circ$, \\
therefore, $\angle MON = 90^\circ + \frac{1}{2} \times 80^\circ = \boxed{130^\circ}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, O is the common endpoint, A, O, B are on the same horizontal straight line, A is on the left side, and B is on the right side. Ray OC extends from O toward the upper left, ray OD extends from O toward the upper right, and ∠COD is the middle included angle. Ray OM is located between OA and OC, and ray ON is located between OB and OD. Reasoning: Let x = ∠AOC = ∠BOD. Because the upper half-plane from OA to OB is a straight angle, ∠AOC + ∠COD + ∠DOB = 180°. Given ∠COD = 80°, therefore x + 80° + x = 180°, solving gives x = 50°. OM bisects ∠AOC, so ∠MOC = x/2 = 25°; ON bisects ∠BOD, so ∠DON = x/2 = 25°. Thus ∠MON = ∠MOC + ∠COD + ∠DON = 25° + 80° + 25° = 130°.
